items.summary: Key TakeawaysArm shares fell 20% in a week in an AI chip selloff that also hit Nvidia and AMD. Arm’s own risk: Nvidia’s recruiters reportedly approached CEO Rene Haas, who leads Arm’s data center chip push.

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Faces Firmware Allegations And Class Action Scrutiny
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices (NasdaqGS:AMD) faces allegations it supplied updated firmware to US-blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems. A short seller's investigative report accused AMD of providing post-blacklist support to IEIT, prompting legal and regulatory scrutiny. Law firms have launched a class-action investigation into AMD for potential securities law violations following the short seller's claims. The reported AMD firmware support for IEIT Systems is a fresh risk signal that...

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman: AI Delivered “Roughly an Additional Year of Progress” on AMD’s Chip in Under 5 Months
items.summary: Key TakeawaysOpenAI’s Greg Brockman says OpenAI’s models delivered roughly an extra year of progress on an AMD chip in under five months. AMD’s edge over Nvidia comes from who did the work: OpenAI, which plans to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs and holds a warrant that pays off as those chips ship.

items.title: Nvidia Must Become a Frontier Lab “Faster Than Frontier Labs Are Becoming Chip Companies.” Nemotron Is Its Head Start
items.summary: Key TakeawaysNvidia shares are down 48% from their high after Jensen Huang’s departure as CEO and a report that the SEC is examining the company’s accounting. Nvidia’s biggest customers are building their own chips with Alphabet and Broadcom, and AI labs are moving code onto chips from AMD.

items.title: Jim Cramer Will “Thank the Shortseller for a Discount” on AMD. Is the China Risk Overblown?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAMD fell 20% in two days, starting with an 8% drop after short seller Hunterbrook reported that a blacklisted Chinese server maker kept using newer AMD firmware. The firmware is for EPYC server CPUs, and Hunterbrook says its findings don’t prove an export violation.
